title: arXiv Physics: notable papers from the 9 October 2026 announcement batch
global_caveat: arXiv provides no official trending chart; this is an inferred, curated ranking based on scientific result, cross-field relevance, and corroborating metadata rather than measured readership. Citation evidence is sparse: Semantic Scholar showed zero citations and zero influential citations for all six papers at the 2026-10-11 00:21 UTC snapshot.

sections.title: Evidence for Normal Neutrino Ordering with Combined Atmospheric Neutrino Experiments
sections.abstract: The authors combine public atmospheric-neutrino data from Super-Kamiokande, IceCube-DeepCore, and KM3NeT/ORCA to constrain oscillation parameters and compare the neutrino mass orderings.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report a preference for normal ordering, excluding inverted ordering at 99.95% confidence (3.3σ) after calibration with pseudoexperiments; they also constrain the CP phase and atmospheric mixing parameters.
sections.evidence_type: Observational; simultaneous analysis of publicly released Super-Kamiokande, IceCube-DeepCore, and KM3NeT/ORCA atmospheric-neutrino samples.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a statistical preference, not a discovery-level resolution. The fit depends on treatment of correlated flux/cross-section and detector systematics; it uses a preview of corrected Super-Kamiokande energy quantiles pending public release.
sections.ranking_evidence: A quantitative 3.3σ preference from a joint fit of three detector datasets, an independent atmospheric-neutrino constraint, and early external discussion; ranked for the result and breadth, not citation volume.

sections.title: Error-Corrected Memory and Logic on a Heavy-Hex Superconducting-Qubit Processor
sections.abstract: The authors demonstrate noise-informed error-correction strategies for memory and logical operations across a 156-qubit heavy-hex superconducting processor, including lattice surgery.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report up to 35% lower logical memory error probabilities and up to 56% gains in stability experiments with noise-informed decoding, defect exclusion, and leakage filtering; post-selection raises reported Bell fidelity above 97%.
sections.evidence_type: Experimental; a 156-qubit IBM heavy-hex superconducting processor, dynamic compass code, noise characterization, and logical-operation experiments.
sections.unique_caveat: Several best results rely on filtering or post-selection, trading usable shots for improved conditional performance; results on one processor do not establish scaling across devices.
sections.ranking_evidence: A 156-qubit hardware experiment spanning memory, measurement-based logic, and lattice surgery addresses defects and error correction on a full monolithic processor.

sections.title: Discovery of Hidden Extragalactic Pulsars in the Parkes Archival Data
sections.abstract: Reprocessing archival Parkes Magellanic-Cloud survey data with deeper candidate folding reveals six pulsars, including five in the Large Magellanic Cloud.
sections.claimed_result: The authors identify five Large Magellanic Cloud pulsars and one foreground Milky Way pulsar toward the Small Magellanic Cloud; their population analysis finds the known Magellanic-Cloud pulsars broadly consistent with Galactic canonical pulsars.
sections.evidence_type: Observational; reanalysis of Parkes Multibeam Magellanic-Cloud survey data using periodicity searches and high-harmonic candidate folding.
sections.unique_caveat: The new sample is small and shaped by survey sensitivity and selection effects; the sixth source is a foreground object, not an SMC pulsar. Unseen-population estimates depend on synthesis assumptions.
sections.ranking_evidence: Six new detections in archival data, including the slowest pulsar known in the Magellanic Clouds, and accepted-for-publication status in ApJ Letters.

sections.title: Listening to the Horizon: Probing Near-Horizon Reflectivity with GW250114
sections.abstract: The authors use a prompt component of GW250114 to search for echoes predicted by a partially reflecting compact-object surface and place an upper bound on reflectivity.
sections.claimed_result: The authors find no evidence for an echo and report a 90% credible upper bound of 0.06 on surface reflectivity, corresponding to less than 0.4% reflected energy, under their echo model.
sections.evidence_type: Observational; template search in quasinormal-mode-filtered GW250114 data, normalized to the observed prompt Direct Wave component.
sections.unique_caveat: The inference is conditional on the echo template and interpretation of the Direct Wave; the paper notes it is unclear whether that component carries horizon information. A null result is not evidence that an exotic compact object exists.
sections.ranking_evidence: A cross-listed gravitational-wave analysis proposes a null test of near-horizon reflectivity using a recently identified signal component, relevant to both gravitational-wave astrophysics and compact-object theory.

sections.title: Transducing quantum-spin-ice correlations into Weyl Fermi-arc transport at a synthetic Kondo lattice interface
sections.abstract: Transport measurements at a Weyl-semimetal/quantum-spin-ice interface show field-dependent anisotropy that the authors associate with quantum-spin-ice correlations imprinted on Fermi-arc transport.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report a sixfold-to-twelvefold-to-sixfold transport-anisotropy sequence at a Eu₂Ir₂O₇/Tb₂Ti₂O₇ interface, absent at the classical-spin-ice interface, and interpret it as quantum correlations affecting Weyl Fermi-arc transport.
sections.evidence_type: Experimental; low-temperature electronic transport across a synthetic Kondo-lattice interface, with a classical-spin-ice comparison.
sections.unique_caveat: The proposed coupling to transverse multipolar degrees of freedom is an interpretation of the transport symmetry contrast, not a direct measurement of those degrees of freedom.
sections.ranking_evidence: The experiment links frustrated quantum magnetism to topological surface transport and compares a quantum-spin-ice interface with a classical-spin-ice control.

sections.title: Cavity Characterization for the Princeton Axion Search
sections.abstract: The authors characterize a tunable, high-Q cavity for the Princeton Axion Search and compare measured electromagnetic modes with simulations to validate its design.
sections.claimed_result: The authors find measured resonance frequencies and the TM010 field profile agree well with simulations over the tested tuning range, supporting the cavity architecture for future sub-μeV axion searches.
sections.evidence_type: Experimental; bead-perturbation measurements and simulations of the cavity planned for a 5 T haloscope.
sections.unique_caveat: Characterizing the cavity validates hardware, not axion detection or DFSZ sensitivity. Initial operation is described for 390–480 MHz, narrower than the full 200–500 MHz target band.
sections.ranking_evidence: Cross-listed across instrumentation, astrophysical methods, and particle experiment; it reports measured mode patterns and uncertainty assessment for an axion-search instrument.
